This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
The petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 10, who are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC, are before this Court.
2. The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband of the defacto complainant.
The accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law.
The accused Nos.4 and 5 are brothers-in-law.
The accused Nos.6 to 9 are the sisters-in- law and the accused No.10 is the brother-in-law.
They subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically.

The cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition by the accused Nos.2 to 10.
3.
The respondent No.2 - defacto complainant though served with notice has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 10 and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State.

5. A perusal of the charge sheet material indicates that, the specific allegation of subjecting the defacto complainant is against the accused No.1, and there is no specific allegation as against the accused Nos.2 to 10 except the omnibus and general allegations.

6. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held that,
the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations, unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, there is no specific allegation against accused Nos.2 to 10, who are the relatives of the accused No.1, except general and omnibus allegations to constitute the above offences.

Hence, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations in the absence of specific allegation is one without substance, and the continuation of criminal proceeding as against the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 10 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
Hobusingh
